clue.text: What's laid out in Roget under "N" …

definitions.text: What's laid out in Roget under "N"

indicators.note: things laid out are spread and rearranged, so the letters are set out in a new order
in a down entry, one piece sitting under another means it comes after it

blocks.note: the two words supply the anagram fodder
taken as written from the clue

explanation.surface: A reader looks up the entries listed under N in Roget's Thesaurus.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, so what sits above the letter N is the element itself. The ellipsis leads into 2 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the element whose chemical symbol is N, so the reworked letters placed above N describe it exactly.

clue.text: … in second revision of Roget, perhaps, looking up "martyr"

indicators.note: a revision changes and reorders text, so the word Roget is rewritten in a new order
in a down entry, a word looking up faces the top of the grid, so it is read bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
the thesaurus compiler's name, rearranged
e.g., for example, signals a 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Down: someone consults a revised edition of Roget's Thesaurus for the word martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 Down, and 'in' simply links the two halves of the sentence. St George, England's patron saint, was martyred around 303 AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George was a Roman soldier executed for his Christian faith, so he is venerated as a martyr.

clue.text: Mould endlessly accreting, cheese stinks

indicators.note: without its end means the final letter of the following word is dropped
to mould something is to reshape it, so the following letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the word loses its last letter, G
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheese gathering mould with age begins to smell badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinks' looks like a verb about the cheese, but it is old British school slang for chemistry, and also the nickname pupils gave the chemistry master.
explanation.definitionFit: In British public-school slang, Stinks was chemistry and the nickname for the master who taught it, a science teacher.

clue.text: Not much change for Putin, put down a lot

blocks.note: a knockout, KO, puts a boxer down
a peck, as in 'a peck of trouble', is a large quantity

explanation.surface: The Russian leader puts down a large amount and gets little change.
explanation.walkthrough: A peck is an old dry measure, and the phrase 'a peck of' means a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck is a hundredth of a rouble, the small Russian coin a Russian like Putin would get as change.

clue.text: Object remains colon replacement?

blocks.note: an end is an aim or object
ash is what remains after burning, as in cremated remains

explanation.surface: Someone objects that the remaining colon should be replaced, as though editing punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colon' suggests the bowel and 'remains' a body, but this is punctuation: a dash can stand in for a colon before an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: The en dash is a punctuation mark that writers often use in place of a colon, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Couples may share these stories about spliffs?

blocks.note: first meaning: bank accounts held in two names
second meaning, whimsical: accounts, or tales, of joints, cannabis cigarettes

explanation.walkthrough: A spliff is a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Married partners commonly keep shared bank accounts, while 'accounts' also means narratives, so tales of cannabis cigarettes fit too.

clue.text: Erstwhile leader only butted in to exchange diamonds for gold

indicators.note: to exchange one thing for another means one letter is swapped out for a different symbol

blocks.note: just means only, as in 'just one'
to butt in is to intrude
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A former leader merely interrupted to trade diamonds for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The last D of the intruding word is replaced by AU.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin Trudeau was Prime Minister of Canada until 2025, so he is a former national leader.

clue.text: Fruit limits after sign post is erected

indicators.note: in a down entry, something erected is stood upright, so it reads from the bottom up
after places the second piece behind the one it follows
post is Latin for after, so this pair comes behind the upended word

blocks.note: to be, or exist, is to live
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a range has limits, its scope

explanation.surface: Some fruit is limited once a signpost has been put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign post' reads as a signpost, but 'sign' and 'post' do separate jobs. 'Is' becomes 'lives' and is upended.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seville orange is a bitter orange grown around Seville in Spain and used for marmalade, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Translated the Legend of Prince Victor in the region of Grenoble

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Isère is the French department whose main city is Grenoble
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone translates a tale of a prince named Victor, set near Grenoble in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' suggests a story, but here it is a motto: the Prince of Wales's motto is the German 'Ich dien'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Wales's heraldic motto 'Ich dien' is German for this phrase, so it is that motto rendered in English.

clue.text: It'll help one seeing 13 fine aluminium parts

indicators.note: the word parts here is a verb: the woman's name is split open so other letters go between

blocks.note: the answer to 13 Down
'fine' as agreement, like saying yes
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Someone spotting a woman's fine aluminium components gets assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun for the aluminium, but it is a verb acting on the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-salve is an ointment for sore eyes, so it helps the person who uses them to see.

clue.text: Recognise individual

blocks.note: first meaning: to acknowledge or admit
second meaning: belonging to oneself, particular

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is 'admit to', as in owning one's mistakes; the adjective sense is 'personal', as in one's own room.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means acknowledge, and as an adjective it means personal or particular to one person.

clue.text: Dancer performing on rigs packs separate tents

indicators.note: performing puts letters into action, working them into a new arrangement
to pack means to hold something inside, so the anagram wraps around other pieces

blocks.note: the two words make the anagram fodder
a ger is a Mongolian felt tent, a yurt; 'separate' means two of them go in different places

explanation.surface: A dancer working on rigs crams in some tents.
explanation.walkthrough: A ger is a Mongolian tent; 'separate' tells you the two go into different spots in the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Rogers was the American film star famous for dancing with Fred Astaire.

clue.text: Spooner's fish and cabbage feed me!

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

blocks.note: hake is a fish and cole is a cabbage or kale; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner calls for a meal of fish and cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of the fish and the cabbage. The definition is the mouth as if speaking for itself: 'feed me!'
explanation.definitionFit: Cakehole is British slang for the mouth, and it is the body part that would demand to be fed.

clue.text: One woman in seven …

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: One woman in a group of seven, the ellipsis leading on to 15 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis.

clue.text: Brown lines change, boring senior painter

indicators.note: boring drills through, so the next item goes into the middle of the other pieces

blocks.note: Sr is the abbreviation for senior
tan is a light brown
ley lines are supposed alignments joining ancient sites
pence are the small coins of loose change

explanation.surface: Brown lines change, a dull older painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like a description of the senior painter, but it puts the brown, lines and change inside SR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Stanley Spencer was an English painter known for his Cookham religious scenes.

clue.text: … Waugh will have joined together with this one?

definitions.text: … Waugh will have joined together with this one?

blocks.clueFragment: Waugh will have joined together with this one?
blocks.note: surface reading: following 13 Down, a woman who has married Waugh
setter's reading: the woman of 13 Down joined to this woman's name makes the novelist's first name, Evelyn

explanation.surface: One woman in seven will have married Waugh, read with 13 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 13 Down: Evelyn Waugh, the novelist, has EVE joined to this answer in his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyn is a woman's name, and EVE plus it spells Evelyn, the first name of the novelist Waugh.

clue.text: See 14
Left artist having acquired it?

indicators.note: having acquired something means it is added on, here placed at the end

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist leaves once someone has bought the work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: a portrait is something left by an artist once the sitter has commissioned it.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is the painting an artist leaves behind, which a buyer or sitter then acquires.

clue.text: Time you enjoy approaching solicitor

blocks.note: nigh means near or approaching
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: A period you like as you near the solicitor's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: A night out is an evening of fun away from home, a pleasant time.

clue.text: See 3
What for Manuel Mark spelt out: "V.I.P."

blocks.note: qué is Spanish for what; Manuel is the Spanish waiter in Fawlty Towers, the British sitcom
NB, nota bene ('mark well'), written as letter names

explanation.surface: Mark spells out the letters V.I.P. for a puzzled Manuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel's catchphrase in Fawlty Towers is 'Qué?'. NB is written out letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee is the most important figure in a group, a very important person.

clue.text: Property close to Providence, say, Rhode Island?

indicators.note: close means the end, so only the finishing letter is used

blocks.note: the final letter
Rhode Island is a US state; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A property near Providence, the capital of Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Providence really is Rhode Island's capital, which keeps the surface geographic.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned by someone, their property.

clue.text: Surprising shout carrying can upset fish

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so it reads from the bottom
carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: boo is shouted to surprise someone
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An unexpected yell knocks over a can of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonito is a fish of the tuna family.

clue.text: See 11
Essential feature picked up in 17s

indicators.note: picked up is read here as lifted backwards, so letters run in the opposite direction
in says only letters lying inside the referenced word are kept, the rest discarded

blocks.note: 17 Down made plural

explanation.surface: An essential feature noticed in portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 17 Down holds the three letters backwards, and the whole clue also defines: art is what every portrait essentially contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Art is the essential quality of any portrait, the skill that makes it a picture.

clue.text: Someone who investigates strengthener of building

blocks.note: tec is short for detective
a tonic is a strengthening medicine

explanation.surface: A building investigator who strengthens structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strengthener of building' reads as one structural item, but 'of building' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonic means relating to construction or architecture, from the Greek for builder.

clue.text: Censure AB assessment

blocks.note: first meaning: a scolding
second meaning: an able seaman, a naval rank below officer
third meaning: an evaluation or score

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two. AB is an able-bodied seaman, and in the Royal Navy a non-officer sailor is a rating.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a reprimand, an enlisted sailor in the navy, and a graded evaluation.

clue.text: Lilliputians responsible for decisions now?

blocks.note: surface reading: the tiny people of Gulliver's Travels in charge of choices
setter's reading: a choice is 'up to' someone, and the Lilliputians are minute, tiny

explanation.surface: The tiny folk of Lilliput are in charge of making decisions now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' here is the adjective meaning tiny, said 'my-NEWT', not the unit of time; the Lilliputians in Gulliver's Travels are six inches tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up-to-the-minute is completely current, of the present moment.
